items.title: NGINX HTTP/2 Use-After-Free: CVE-2026-123633
items.summary: Unit 42 reports on CVE-2026-123633, a use‑after‑free vulnerability in NGINX HTTP/2. The analysis covers affected versions, sanitizer test results, and provides patch guidance.

items.title: An Unclassified CIA System Was Breached in a Cyberattack, AP Source Says
items.summary: SecurityWeek reports that an unclassified CIA system was breached, but the scope of data compromised and the attacker remain unknown.

items.title: Satellites Have a Ground-Level Cybersecurity Problem
items.summary: Ground‑based infrastructure supporting satellite services is increasingly vulnerable, raising concerns as the space race intensifies.

items.title: Unclassified intel system hit by hackers, affecting CIA, ODNI
items.summary: CyberScoop confirms a hack of an unclassified intelligence system used by the CIA and ODNI, with no other systems currently at risk.

items.title: Webworm APT Slithers Into Networks With Customized SoftEther VPN
items.summary: The China‑aligned Webworm APT modifies open‑source SoftEther VPN to remove detection artifacts, enabling stealthy network infiltration.

items.title: Rackspace shuts down Spot cloud platform after security breach
items.summary: Rackspace is shutting down its Spot cloud platform after a breach that exposed customer Kubernetes clusters and secrets, giving users until December 8 to migrate.

items.title: 'God Mode' Flaws Could Wreak Border-Control Havoc
items.summary: Vulnerabilities in several countries’ online visa and immigration systems could allow attackers to disrupt traveler entry into Nigeria, Ethiopia, Zambia, Sri Lanka, Fiji, and Ghana.

items.title: Colorado says cyberattack took down myColorado app, warns 150,000 had data stolen
items.summary: A cyberattack disabled Colorado’s myColorado app, potentially compromising data of 150,000 users who use the platform for digital ID and state services.
items.source: The Record from Recorded Future News

items.title: New Inception extortion gang launches large-scale vishing campaign
items.summary: The newly formed Inception extortion group is conducting a large‑scale vishing campaign targeting single sign‑on credentials of multiple global brands.

items.title: 'We are not ShinyHunters,' says criminal hacking crew that looks and acts just like ShinyHunters
items.summary: A hacking group claims it is not ShinyHunters, despite similarities in appearance and behavior.

items.title: California privacy agency director Kemp to leave after two-year tenure
items.summary: The director of the California Privacy Protection Agency announced his departure after a two‑year tenure that saw the launch of a first‑of‑its‑kind consumer opt‑out platform for data sharing.
items.source: The Record from Recorded Future News

items.title: Turnitin discloses cyberattack affecting customer-facing systems
items.summary: Turnitin’s CEO reported unauthorized activity on customer‑facing systems and said the company is investigating the impact of the breach.

items.title: Radware discloses breach exposing customer cloud access keys
items.summary: Radware disclosed that attackers accessed customer account details and cloud access keys through an exposed internal Cloud WAF management API.

items.title: Lawmakers warn ID verification companies to bolster security after September hack
items.summary: Lawmakers urged identity verification companies to strengthen security after the September IDscan data breach.
items.source: The Record from Recorded Future News

items.title: Patel mum on FBI crime info database hack, citing ongoing investigation
items.summary: The FBI remains silent on the National Crime Information Center breach, citing an ongoing investigation.

items.title: Iran-Aligned Volant Manticore Uses IPFS-Based KuboShell Backdoor in Espionage Campaigns
items.summary: Iran‑aligned group Volant Manticore uses the KuboShell backdoor, which leverages IPFS for command‑and‑control, in espionage campaigns against telecoms, airlines, and critical infrastructure in Cyprus.

items.title: VMware Updates Patch Critical ESX, vCenter Vulnerabilities
items.summary: VMware released critical patches for ESX and vCenter vulnerabilities. The fixes address an authentication bypass in vCenter and potential code execution on ESX hosts. The update mitigates high‑risk security flaws.

items.title: ShinyHunters claims to return after FBI arrests, uses old PGP keys as proof
items.summary: ShinyHunters extortion group claims to have returned after FBI arrests. They posted on a new data‑leak site and cited old PGP keys as proof. The claim follows a series of arrests targeting alleged members.

items.title: New Inception Extortion Brand Tied to SSO Vishing Campaign
items.summary: New Inception extortion brand linked to an SSO vishing campaign. Okta and ReversingLabs identified the threat targeting employee credentials via social engineering. The campaign exploits single sign‑on vulnerabilities.

items.title: European Commission confirms data theft in EU Academy breach
items.summary: European Commission confirmed a data theft from its EU Academy online learning hub. Attackers accessed personal data of an undisclosed number of users. The breach highlights the need for stronger security controls.

items.title: Hackers compromise Check Point Servers in 22 organizations
items.summary: Threat actors compromised 22 Check Point Security management servers across multiple organizations. The attack exploited several vulnerabilities to gain unauthorized access. The incident underscores the importance of patching.

items.title: Carnegie Endowment for International Peace says third-party breach leaked donation info
items.summary: Carnegie Endowment for International Peace reported a third‑party breach that leaked donor information. The cyberattack targeted vendor Soapbox Engage, exposing sensitive donor data. The incident emphasizes third‑party risk.
items.source: The Record from Recorded Future News

items.title: How to compare MDR providers when every proposal looks promising
items.summary: Choosing a managed detection and response provider requires careful evaluation. Key questions include which systems are monitored, analyst investigation procedures, and response protocols. Clear criteria help avoid costly missteps.

items.title: Police disrupt 57 illegal streaming services with 7.3 million visits
items.summary: Law enforcement from 11 countries shut down 57 illegal streaming services that operated hundreds of websites. The operation disrupted over 7.3 million annual visits. The effort demonstrates cross‑border cooperation.

items.title: CISA warns of exploited N-able bug as company restores email platform
items.summary: CISA warned of an exploited vulnerability in N‑able's email security platform. Government agencies were urged to patch before Thanksgiving. The bug could compromise email filtering and threat protection.
items.source: The Record from Recorded Future News

items.title: McDonald's Japan data breach exposes customer location information
items.summary: McDonald's Japan disclosed a data breach affecting its official smartphone app database. Attackers accessed customer location and other sensitive information. The incident highlights the importance of mobile app security.

items.title: GTA 6 hacker sentenced to seven years and released the same day
items.summary: Arion Kurtaj, 21, was sentenced to seven years in prison for leaking Grand Theft Auto VI footage and was released on licence the same day.

items.title: VMware vCenter Hit by Another Critical 9.8-Rated Auth Bypass Flaw After Zero-Day Exploitation
items.summary: Broadcom released patches for 23 vulnerabilities in VMware products, including CVE‑2026‑123903, a 9.8‑rated flaw that allows authentication bypass in the Directory Service.

items.title: Okta Links ShinyHunters-Associated Vishing Group to New INCEPTION Data Leak Site
items.summary: Okta identified threat cluster O‑UNC‑053, linked to the ShinyHunters crew, now operating under the name INCEPTION and using vishing to harvest credentials.

items.title: Rapid7 Analysis: VMware vCenter SRP Authentication Bypass to Root (CVE-2026-123890)
items.summary: CVE‑2026‑123890 enables an unauthenticated attacker to capture an SRP session key during an admin login and complete the login without a password via DCE/RPC on port 2012.

items.title: McDonald’s Japan discloses breach exposing customer purchase and location data
items.summary: McDonald’s Japan disclosed a breach that exposed customers’ purchase histories and mobile device location data.
items.source: The Record from Recorded Future News

items.title: ShinyHunters-linked crew resurfaces on new leak site
items.summary: Okta reports that the ShinyHunters crew has moved to a new leak site called Inception, continuing social engineering and credential harvesting since March 2026.

items.title: Hackers Found a Way Around GitHub SHA Pinning. This Webinar Explains How to Close the Gap
items.summary: Hackers bypassed GitHub Actions SHA pinning by inserting malicious code into Trivy, masquerading as the official GitHub checkout tool.

items.title: CrowdStrike splashes $44B on Zscaler, customers brace for the bill
items.summary: CrowdStrike announced a $44 billion investment in Zscaler, raising concerns about higher costs and potential vendor lock‑in for customers.

items.title: Google Researcher Shows How a Single Bit Change in .NET Files Bypassed Windows Code Integrity
items.summary: Project Zero researcher James Forshaw showed that a single bit change in a .NET file can bypass Windows code integrity and Oracle VirtualBox hardening, tracked as CVE‑2026‑87268.

items.title: 2027 SOC Budget Reset: 5 Priorities to Cut Costs and Reduce Cyber Risk
items.summary: ANY.RUN estimates that SOC teams could recover 450 analyst hours per 1,000 alerts by speeding threat analysis and IOC research, offering a cost‑saving opportunity.

items.title: OpenAI and Cisco Release Open-Source Tool to Shield Unpatched Linux Systems
items.summary: OpenAI and Cisco released Shirudo, an open‑source tool that blocks exploitation of known vulnerabilities on live Linux systems. It allows administrators to buy time for patching without restarting the system.

items.title: 1.5 Million Impacted by Data Breach at South Korean Electric Company KEPCO
items.summary: Hackers accessed KEPCO’s customer portal and supplier management platform, compromising personal data of approximately 1.5 million individuals. The breach was reported by SecurityWeek.

items.title: Tomorrow’s quantum threat is today’s open door
items.summary: The article argues that post‑quantum cryptography should be added to the roadmap, but current operational technology faces more immediate, basic threats that require urgent action.

items.title: Microsoft Fixes Azure API Management Classic Flaw as Actor Targets Customer Secrets
items.summary: Microsoft patched a vulnerability in Azure API Management that could expose access tokens and secrets. An unknown actor targeted customers in Norway, including energy firms, seeking these credentials.

items.title: Elecbrakes Bluetooth Vulnerabilities Expose Trailers to Forced Braking
items.summary: Critical Bluetooth flaws in Elecbrakes trailer controllers could allow nearby attackers to trigger forced braking. This vulnerability could lead to accidents on the road.

items.title: Peninsula Energy Halts Trading After Cyber Incident Hits US Uranium Mine
items.summary: Peninsula Energy halted trading after a cyber incident at its Wyoming uranium project temporarily disrupted operations. The company notified the ASX of the incident.

items.title: LaLiga Says Football Fans’ Personal Data Stolen
items.summary: LaLiga disclosed a breach that exposed personally identifiable information of its football fans. The incident was reported by the league.

items.title: GlobeTopper faces up to $2.5 million in lost revenue after hackers steal $70,000 in gift cards
items.summary: Hackers breached GlobeTopper, stole API credentials, and redeemed about $70,000 in gift cards without authorization. The company estimates up to $2.5 million in lost revenue.

items.title: WHMCS SQL Injection Could Expose Customer Data and Admin Password Hashes without Login
items.summary: A SQL injection flaw in WHMCS’s shopping cart allows unauthenticated users to retrieve customer records and administrator password hashes from the database. The issue was disclosed by the vendor.

items.title: Orgs that leak data 'prioritize corporate interests over customers' says Have I Been Pwned’s Troy Hunt
items.summary: Troy Hunt notes that organizations leaking data often prioritize corporate interests over customers. He describes a pattern of denial, bargaining, delay, legal threats, and blaming Hunt.

items.title: Cisco and OpenAI pitch eBPF kernel plugins as the way to tame the patchpocalypse
items.summary:
Cisco and OpenAI propose eBPF kernel plugins to deploy compensating controls quickly during patch cycles.
The Shirudo project aims to generate these controls automatically.
This approach targets the ongoing patchpocalypse.

items.title: Hackers breach Austrian Foreign Ministry website, access diplomats' contact details
items.summary: Hackers accessed the Austrian Foreign Ministry website, retrieving names and official contact information of employees at Vienna headquarters and diplomatic missions abroad.
items.source: The Record from Recorded Future News

items.title: LaLiga hacked: Spain’s top football league confirms theft of fans’ personal data
items.summary: Spain’s LaLiga confirmed a cyberattack that stole personal data from fans. The breach impacted the league’s digital services and those of several Spanish clubs.
items.source: The Record from Recorded Future News

items.title: Cybersecurity jobs available right now: November 24, 2026
items.summary:
A remote Applied Cyber, Detections position in the USA focuses on detection operations.
Responsibilities include optimizing detection logic, automating alert triage, and investigating gaps.
The role also supports customer onboarding and configuration.

items.title: Industrial Serial Gateways Broadcast That They're Insecure
items.summary:
Many industrial serial gateways publicly disclose whether they are protected by authentication.
This transparency reveals that numerous OT access devices lack proper security.
The issue highlights a widespread vulnerability.

items.title: Inception - possibly a ShinyHunters reboot - claims seven victims in a week
items.summary:
A new phishing group, possibly a reboot of ShinyHunters, claims seven victims in a week.
They emphasize the threat of voice phishing attempts.
Security teams are advised to remain vigilant.

items.title: South Korea’s power giant KEPCO confirms data breach impacting 1.5 million
items.summary:
Korea Electric Power Corporation (KEPCO) confirmed a breach affecting 1.5 million records.
The attacker accessed customer, employee, and contractor data on two internal systems.
The incident underscores the need for stronger network defenses.

items.title: US Cyber Director Pick Signals Shift Toward Expertise
items.summary:
President Trump appointed Kirsten Davies as Acting National Cyber Director.
Her industry experience is seen as a shift toward expertise.
The appointment comes amid recent outages and geopolitical tensions.

items.title: Microsoft Azure flaw exploited to steal customers' API credentials
items.summary:
A flaw in Azure API Management Classic tiers was exploited to steal stored API credentials.
Norwegian authorities link the vulnerability to attacks on energy companies.
Microsoft has warned affected customers to review their security settings.

items.title: Bluetooth brakes are broken as researchers find anyone can control them
items.summary:
Researchers discovered that any user can control certain Elecbrakes Bluetooth brakes.
Security fixes exist for two models, but an older controller remains vulnerable.
The finding raises concerns about vehicle safety.

items.title: Spanish LaLiga confirms hackers stole soccer fans’ personal data
items.summary:
LaLiga disclosed a data breach that exposed personal information of users and affiliated clubs.
The breach involved the league’s services.
Details of the affected data remain limited.

items.title: Indicted Kosovo credit card theft suspect extradited to US
items.summary:
Hektor Avdyli, indicted for credit card theft, was extradited to the United States.
A hard drive in his possession contained millions of payment card numbers.
The extradition follows international cooperation on cybercrime.

items.title: FBI reportedly facing second data breach involving National Crime Information Center
items.summary: The FBI is investigating a data breach of the National Crime Information Center. The database holds information on criminals, fugitives, and missing persons used by U.S. law enforcement.
items.source: The Record from Recorded Future News

items.title: Critical Cisco remote code execution bug under attack
items.summary: Cisco's critical remote code execution vulnerability is being actively exploited. CISA and F6 have issued alerts after a proof‑of‑concept exploit was released publicly.

items.title: Behind the Alias: How One Researcher Unmasked a Decade of Ransomware Actors
items.summary: A new framework enables security teams to trace ransomware operators back to their source. The study shows ransomware activity remains persistent.

items.title: Webworm Suspected of Modifying SoftEther VPN to Evade Detection and Hide Remote Access
items.summary: The threat actor Webworm is believed to have modified the open‑source SoftEther VPN Bridge. The custom version hides from security tools and provides covert remote access.

items.title: Bulgaria evicts cyber snoops who lurked inside government networks for 5 years
items.summary: Bulgaria removed intruders who had accessed government networks for five years, during which they downloaded over 130 GB of data amid security lapses.

items.title: Kirsten Davies to become national cyber director nominee, Jay Clayton takes acting director job
items.summary: Kirsten Davies has been nominated to become the National Cyber Director, while Jay Clayton will serve as acting director until the appointment is finalized.

items.title: GlobeTopper loses $2.5 million after hackers steal $70k in gift cards
items.summary: GlobeTopper suffered a cyberattack that disrupted operations, resulting in an estimated $2.5 million loss and the theft of $70 000 in digital gift cards.

items.title: Azure Flaw Exploited to Target Secrets at Norwegian Energy Firms
items.summary: A Microsoft Azure API Management flaw was exploited to target secrets at Norwegian energy companies, prompting Microsoft to close the vulnerability.

items.title: Norway says hackers exploited Microsoft security flaw to attack energy firms Equinor, Skagerak Energi
items.summary: Norwegian authorities reported that a Microsoft cloud security vulnerability was used to compromise credentials at Equinor and Skagerak Energi.
items.source: The Record from Recorded Future News

items.title: CrowdStrike to Acquire Zscaler in Record $44 Billion Deal
items.summary: CrowdStrike announced a $43.9 billion acquisition of Zscaler, adding network security capabilities to its portfolio.

items.title: 'Overwhelming' support leads Trump to lock in Davies for national cyber czar
items.summary: President Trump confirmed Kirsten Davies as the national cyber director after receiving strong support for her nomination.
items.source: The Record from Recorded Future News

items.title: ⚡ Weekly Recap: VMware 0-Day, Java4Shell, NGINX2Root, Ruby2Shell, and a Whole Lot of Shell Trouble
items.summary: The week highlighted multiple vulnerabilities, including VMware 0‑Day, Java4Shell, NGINX2Root, and Ruby2Shell, illustrating how small openings can lead to larger breaches.

items.title: N-able Patches Critical Flaw Disclosed After Mail Assure Cyberattack
items.summary: N‑able released a patch for a critical flaw after a Mail Assure cyberattack, restoring access to affected services and monitoring environments.

items.title: GL.iNet cloud compromise hits routers and KVMs, older backdoors also found
items.summary:
Attackers compromised GL.iNet’s GoodCloud remote‑management service and installed malware on routers and KVM devices.
Investigation is ongoing and older backdoors were also discovered.

items.title: phpAfterShell Vulnerability Revives PHP2Shell’s Attack Path
items.summary:
The phpAfterShell vulnerability allows an attacker to trigger data deserialization and remote code execution when a session overwrite is interrupted.
It re‑opens the attack path used by PHP2Shell.

items.title: US Lawmakers Propose CISA Board to Review Major Cyber Incidents
items.summary:
Two U.S. congressmen have proposed creating a cyber‑incident review board within the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency.
The board would evaluate major cyber incidents.

items.title: Microsoft testing fix for Windows 11 Bluetooth audio quality drops
items.summary:
Microsoft is testing a fix for a long‑standing Windows 11 issue that causes significant audio quality drops on Bluetooth headphones.
The problem has affected many users.

items.title: GL.iNet Routers, KVMs Compromised via Remote Management Service Flaw
items.summary:
A flaw in GoodCloud enabled attackers to push malware to GL.iNet routers and KVMs.
Remediation requires installing new firmware.

items.title: Critical binary-parser Flaw Enables JavaScript Injection via Malicious Parser Definitions
items.summary:
CVE‑2026‑134814 is a critical code‑injection flaw in the binary‑parser library.
It lets attackers execute arbitrary JavaScript via malicious parser definitions in versions before 2.3.1.

items.title: Cleverbridge alerts customers that hackers stole their credit card and CVV numbers
items.summary:
Hackers breached Cleverbridge and stole payment card data, including credit‑card numbers and CVV codes.
The company has not identified which of its clients were affected.

items.title: CrowdStrike to acquire Zscaler for $43.9 billion
items.summary:
CrowdStrike has agreed to acquire Zscaler in an all‑stock deal valued at approximately $43.9 billion.
Zscaler shareholders will receive 1.135 CrowdStrike shares per Zscaler share.

items.title: Hackers Exploit Critical ScreenConnect Flaw to Hijack MSP Technician PCs Without Warning
items.summary:
Threat actors exploited CVE‑2026‑84869 in ConnectWise ScreenConnect to transfer and execute malicious payloads on MSP technician PCs.
Activity was observed on November 12.

items.title: Norway links energy firm cyberattacks to critical Azure API Management flaw
items.summary:
Microsoft reports mitigation for a critical Azure API Management flaw.
Norwegian energy firm attributes recent cyberattacks to this vulnerability and advises administrators to rotate secrets.

items.title: N-able Discloses Critical Mail Assure Vulnerability Found During Breach Investigation
items.summary: N‑Able disclosed a critical SSRF flaw (CVE‑2026‑134624) found while investigating a breach of its Mail Assure and SpamExperts Hosted Cloud services. The vulnerability allowed users with high‑level API access to open connections to internal systems of their choosing.

items.title: Cisco Expressway vulnerability exploited to breach internal networks (CVE-2026-76466)
items.summary: Attackers exploited a critical vulnerability (CVE‑2026‑76466) in Cisco Expressway gateways to breach organizations. The U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency added the flaw to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog.

items.title: Call center operator gets 8 years for helping scam 30,000 Americans
items.summary: A Peruvian call‑center operator received an eight‑year prison sentence for facilitating a fraud scheme that stole millions from more than 30,000 Spanish‑speaking U.S. residents.

items.title: Cleverbridge admits attackers stole customers' credit card and CVV numbers. Yep, you read that right
items.summary: Cleverbridge confirmed that attackers stole customers’ credit‑card numbers and CVV codes. The company has not disclosed how the data was captured or the scale of the breach.

items.title: BadBox 3.0 Ad Fraud Operation Generating 40 Billion Daily Bid Requests Disrupted
items.summary: The BadBox 3.0 ad‑fraud operation, which used backdoors on low‑cost consumer devices, was disrupted after generating 40 billion daily bid requests for ad fraud and residential proxy services.

items.title: SAP NetWeaver, Cisco Expressway Flaws Exploited in Attacks
items.summary: Threat actors exploited flaws in SAP NetWeaver and Cisco Expressway to leak or modify server information and execute commands with root privileges.

items.title: CrowdStrike to Acquire Zscaler in $43.9 Billion Deal
items.summary: CrowdStrike announced its acquisition of Zscaler for $43.9 billion, with the combined company expected to exceed $10 billion in annual recurring revenue.

items.title: WPIDE ≤ 3.6.4 — CSRF Nonce Bypass Leading to Unauthenticated RCE (CVE-2026-124251)
items.summary: WPIDE versions ≤3.6.4 contain a CSRF nonce bypass (CVE‑2026‑124251) that enables unauthenticated remote code execution.

items.title: Cleverbridge Confirms Customers’ Payment Card Data Breached
items.summary: Cleverbridge confirmed that customers’ payment card data, including card numbers and security codes, were breached, posing an immediate fraud risk to affected individuals.

items.title: Attackers exploited Microsoft Entra Connect Health flaw to access tenant data
items.summary: Attackers exploited a vulnerability in the Microsoft Entra Connect Health API to read technical contact email addresses and configuration details of Entra tenants.

items.title: Black Friday, red flags: too-good-to-be-true deals hiding real threats
items.summary: Cybercriminals are targeting Black Friday shoppers with phishing, scams, and malware. They focus on fake sales, GTA VI, wellness schemes, and spam campaigns.

items.title: Critical Cisco Expressway Flaw Exploited in Attacks
items.summary: Cisco Expressway is affected by CVE-2026-76466, a CVSS 9.8 flaw. The vulnerability is actively exploited in attacks.

items.title: Badbox Returns to Spread Ad Fraud and Proxyjacking Payloads
items.summary: Badbox 3.0 is generating 40 billion ad bid requests per day. It spreads ad fraud and proxyjacking payloads.

items.title: Hackers Exploit Critical ASP.NET Anti-CSRF Library Flaw Allowing Unauthenticated RCE
items.summary: CVE-2026-131914 allows unauthenticated remote code execution in Idunno.AntiCsrf.dll 0.9.1.0 and 0.9.1 Beta. Users should stop using the library.

items.title: Microsoft confirms Windows printing issues affecting Forcepoint users
items.summary: Microsoft confirmed that the KB5132043 Windows 11 hotpatch causes printing issues on systems running Forcepoint DLP software.

items.title: Hackers Exploited GL.iNet Cloud Flaw to Install Malware on Routers and KVM Devices
items.summary: A flaw in GL.iNet GoodCloud remote management was used to install malware on routers and KVM devices. The company fixed the vulnerability and blocked the attack vector.

items.title: When Microsoft, Apple, and the FAA can't keep it up, it's a system of a down
items.summary: The article examines repeated outages affecting Microsoft, Apple, and the FAA. It calls for radical systemic solutions.

items.title: Infected TV boxes in BADBOX 3.0 rent out their owners’ home internet
items.summary: Infected low‑cost TV boxes operated by BADBOX 3.0 produced 40 billion ad bid requests daily, over 4 % of CTV traffic and triple the volume of VASTFLUX.

items.title: VirtualBox Process Hardening on Windows 2026 Edition: What’s a Single Bit Between Friends?
items.summary: Research uncovered three ways to bypass VirtualBox's kernel driver protection on Windows. The flaw could allow privilege escalation on host systems.

items.title: CISA flags critical Cisco RCE flaw as actively exploited in attacks
items.summary: CISA warned that a patched Cisco Expressway RCE vulnerability is being exploited in the wild. Federal agencies are urged to patch immediately.

items.title: Yes, but securely: A cancer institute’s answer to shadow IT in research
items.summary: INT’s Director discusses preventing shadow IT while maintaining operations. The focus is on collaboration with partner hospitals and cyberattack protection.

items.title: Google claims last week’s critical VMware bug was under attack in September
items.summary: Google reports that the critical VMware vCenter bug was exploited in September. China‑linked ARMORY CASTLE used the flaw to deploy five custom malware tools.
